correctness.rationale: For q=0 the semigroup is ordinary, and for a=2 the even-plus-upper-odd form is manifestly Arf. For q>=1,a>=3 Shor Proposition 3.4 gives the high gaps h=g+ka. Each such h has h-1,h-2 in S, so the first Arf operator must add h; the resulting set is Arf by a largest-element case split. This gives both inclusions, exact genus/conductor/index, and the g-parity count. Standalone finite generator/saturation/triple checks cross-checked 3,760 pairs but are not used as the infinite argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General closure algorithms and fixed-multiplicity Arf parametrizations provide a way to calculate cases, not a published uniform reflective-family theorem. Çelik explicitly treats two-generator symmetric prime-multiplicity families: they can overlap particular reflective examples, but do not cover all multiplicities or all reflective semigroups. A general algorithm might indirectly imply any instance once executed; the symbolic all-parameter formula and the at-most-one-step bound are different coverage.

value.rationale: Arf closure is a canonical singularity-related numerical-semigroup invariant. For a naturally defined genus-symmetry class, the theorem gives an explicit formula, full classification of Arf cases, exact genus and conductor changes, and a uniform one-step stabilization threshold across infinitely many genera and multiplicities, not an isolated computation or arbitrary slice. It identifies a sharp structural difference between multiplicity two and larger multiplicities.
